measureRecords.whatItDoes: Beginning January 1, 2027, let Gypsum collect and use a 4% lodging tax that Eagle County currently collects and uses, instead of the county receiving it. The tax applies to rooms or accommodations provided for fewer than 30 consecutive days. The question authorizes $200,000 in the first full fiscal year and whatever the tax produces later. Uses could include town-maintained roads, parks, recreation facilities and other public improvements, and events the town sponsors, funds or assists. Tax revenue and earnings could be retained and spent outside the stated constitutional and other legal revenue limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the town’s collection and use of this 4% lodging tax and the proposed revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this proposed town lodging tax and transfer of proceeds through this measure.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Add 0.5 percentage points to Basalt’s sales-tax rate beginning January 1, 2027, for no more than 20 years. The question authorizes up to $1.7 million in the first full fiscal year, 2027, and whatever the tax generates later. Money would pay for acquiring, planning, building, operating, maintaining, repairing and replacing public-services facilities and related infrastructure and equipment. The town could retain and spend this revenue and investment income outside the stated constitutional and other legal revenue and spending limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the temporary sales-tax increase for the stated facilities and equipment, and its revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this additional sales tax or its revenue-limit exception.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorize up to $5.6 million in additional school property taxes in 2026 for collection in 2027. In later years, this levy and other voter-approved general-fund levies together would raise the maximum allowed by the cited state school-funding law as it stood on July 1, 2026. Money would go to the district’s general fund for education, including teacher and staff pay, recruitment and retention, academic results and closing achievement gaps. All spending of the new revenue must appear in the district’s annual independent audit, published on its website and reviewed by its school board. The levy would be additional to existing general-fund property taxes.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the additional school property taxes and the required public audit reporting.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this additional school property-tax levy through this measure.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Waive the district’s 5.25% property-tax growth limit for all future property-tax years. For fiscal year 2026 and later, let the district retain and spend all revenue it is legally authorized by law or contract to receive, including taxes, tax-increment revenue, fees, service charges, gifts and grants. These receipts would be exempt from the stated constitutional spending and revenue limits, the other cited property-tax growth limit in later years, and other current or future laws limiting district revenue or spending. The question sets no new tax rate.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the permanent property-tax growth-limit waiver and broader authority to retain and spend legally authorized revenue.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve these proposed revenue-limit waivers through this measure.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Create a 0.55% district sales tax, or 55 cents per $100, beginning January 1, 2027, on transactions subject to state sales tax, excluding groceries and other exempt items. The question authorizes $1,518,000 in the first full fiscal year and whatever the tax raises later. Money would pay for fire protection and emergency services, including a year-round wildland-fire division, wildfire prevention and fuels reduction, fire suppression, emergency medical and rescue services, equipment and facilities, and related staffing, operating, maintenance and capital costs. All district revenue could be retained and spent despite legal revenue limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the new sales tax for the stated services and the revenue-limit exception for all district revenue.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this additional sales tax or the proposed exception to district revenue limits.
